        Steps:
        1. clone the repo git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
        2. analyse the contents of the repo and create following.

function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a **step‑by‑step guide** you can copy‑paste into your terminal (or adapt to your own workflow).  
I’ll also give you the exact file contents you’ll need to create/modify in the repo.

> ⚠️ **Prerequisites**  
> * You must have `git`, `docker`, and `kubectl` installed locally.  
> * You need a Docker Hub account (or another registry) and the credentials stored as secrets in the repo (`DOCKER_USERNAME`, `DOCKER_PASSWORD`).  
> * If you’re using GitHub Actions, make sure the repo has “Actions” enabled.

---

## 1️⃣ Clone the repository

```bash
# Replace <your‑ssh‑key> with the key that has write access to the repo
git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

---

## 2️⃣ Analyse & create/update files

### 2.1 Dockerfile

Create or overwrite `Dockerfile` at the repo root:

```Dockerfile
# Dockerfile
FROM node:18-alpine AS builder

WORKDIR /app

# Copy only the metadata first so we can cache dependencies
COPY package*.json ./

# Install production dependencies
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy the rest of the source
COPY . .

# Build step (if you have a build script)
# RUN npm run build   # Uncomment if you have a build step

# Final stage
FROM node:18-alpine

WORKDIR /app

# Copy built artifacts from builder
COPY --from=builder /app .

EXPOSE 3000

CMD ["node", "app.js"]
```

> **Why this Dockerfile?**  
> * Uses a multi‑stage build to keep the image small.  
> * Installs only production deps (`npm ci --only=production`).  
> * Exposes port 3000 – the default port used by many Node apps.

### 2.2 Kubernetes YAML

Create a file `k8s/deployment.yaml` (you can create a `k8s` folder if it doesn’t exist):

```yaml
# k8s/deployment.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: <YOUR_DOCKERHUB_USER>/nodejs-welcome:latest   # <-- replace with your image
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer          # Change to NodePort/ClusterIP if you prefer
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80                  # External port
    targetPort: 3000          # Container port
```

> **Tip:** If you’re deploying to a cluster that doesn’t support `LoadBalancer` (e.g., minikube), change `type` to `NodePort`.

### 2.3 GitHub Actions workflow

Create `.github/workflows/docker-build.yml`:

```yaml
name: Build & Push Docker Image

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build-and-push:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - name: Checkout source
      uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Set up Docker Buildx
      uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

    - name: Log in to Docker Hub
      uses: docker/login-action@v3
      with:
        username: ${{ secrets.DOCKER_USERNAME }}
        password: ${{ secrets.DOCKER_PASSWORD }}

    - name: Cache npm dependencies
      uses: actions/cache@v3
      with:
        path: ~/.npm
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-npm-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}
        restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-npm-

    - name: Build and push Docker image
      uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
      with:
        context: .
        push: true
        tags: ${{ secrets.DOCKER_USERNAME }}/nodejs-welcome:latest
```

> **What this workflow does**  
> * Triggers on pushes to `main`.  
> * Caches npm modules to speed up builds.  
> * Builds the image defined by the Dockerfile and pushes it to Docker Hub under the tag `latest`.

---

## 3️⃣ Add all changed files to git

```bash
git add Dockerfile k8s/deployment.yaml .github/workflows/docker-build.yml
```

If you want to see what’s staged:

```bash
git status
```

---

## 4️⃣ Commit & push

```bash
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, K8s manifests, and CI workflow"
git push origin main
```

> After pushing, the GitHub Actions workflow will automatically run.  
> Once it succeeds, you’ll have a fresh image on Docker Hub ready to deploy.

---

### Optional: Deploy to a cluster

```bash
# Apply the manifests
kubectl apply -f k8s/deployment.yaml
```

Check the rollout status:

```bash
kubectl rollout status deployment/nodejs-welcome-deployment
```

And get the external IP (for LoadBalancer services):

```bash
kubectl get svc nodejs-welcome-service
```

---

That’s it! 🎉  
Feel free to tweak the Dockerfile (add a `build` script, set environment variables, etc.) or the Kubernetes manifests (add resource limits, liveness/readiness probes, etc.) to suit your needs.
